propositions: A fake transport masks failure modes that only appear against a real tracker: real JQL over multiple projects, per-project key allocation, and cross-project isolation; live rehearsal against ephemeral Jira DC instance is necessary to validate these
Non-existent project keys configured in the mapping cause the inbound fetcher to fail-closed and abort the entire pass (no per-project try/except), while fake transport incorrectly returns empty

Dry-run gating via `bridge preview` must verify that each mutation targets only projects in its intended scope with empty intersection against all other configured projects before `bridge sync` applies mutations
Scratch projects are created with pinned template, provisioned capabilities verified pre-scenario, and deterministically torn down on every exit path including mid-run failures
A project configured but never created in Jira must be rejected fail-closed with no mutation applied, while a real empty project returns no issues and succeeds
All three repo configurations (one/two/zero repos) must produce expected repos on inbound ingestion and correct routing on outbound mutations across isolated throwaway projects
